title: Why MCP revenue is still zero
conclusion: Engineering progress has outrun commercial validation. The strongest explanation for zero revenue is insufficient qualified discovery and an unproven reason to pay for the upgrade.
accountability: Earlier sprints prioritized adding servers, releases and automated checks before establishing repeat buyer use and a paid upgrade. That was the wrong sequence for a revenue goal. More output was repeatedly treated as progress toward sales without evidence that buyers were arriving.

findings.title: Discovery is too small to support a revenue expectation
findings.evidence: Google supplied zero measured clicks in the finalized 28-date window. GitHub reports 58 views and 32 unique clients for October 2–15; those are not qualified customers. Registry rows, search positions and downloads do not establish buyer acquisition. Fresh inspection finds the two focus products discovered but not indexed; the guide remains unknown.
findings.implication: Publishing another server adds supply without a demonstrated way to bring buyers to it.

findings.title: Usage and repeat value are still unproven
findings.evidence: The new hosted instrument records zero ordinary successful business calls and zero ordinary checkout handoffs, alongside 13 probe successes. Its first record is October 16 at 08:32 UTC: roughly 15 hours of evidence, not weeks. It excludes local usage and unresolved older tokens; deferred events can drop.
findings.implication: We cannot claim that nobody used any tool, or that an installed audience exists and wants an upgrade. Qualified buyer trials and repeat use remain unknown.

findings.title: The paid benefit may be too weak for occasional users
findings.evidence: Duplicate invoice review gives full diagnostics, paging and CSV export away free. The $19 upgrade removes the three-saved-report cap. A user can complete a one-off review without paying.
findings.implication: Test whether real users need ongoing saved reports. A purchase button and a low price do not establish willingness to pay. Do not arbitrarily damage the useful free tier.

findings.title: Distribution work has not produced a proven buyer channel
findings.status: Dated evidence, not a full channel census
findings.evidence: One Finance directory submission remains pending in the October 16 receipt. The new Glama page was 404/account-gated. The October 16 outreach audit found 18 manual targets, zero eligible email recipients and zero sends.
findings.implication: These are publication attempts and configuration work; no qualified pipeline has been established. Resend access alone does not supply an audience.

findings.title: Engineering counters obscured the commercial problem
findings.evidence: Server count, tests, archive downloads, token IDs and synthetic recommendations were easier to increase than paid use. The old $38 sales claim also mixed this project with another storefront.
findings.implication: Lead the dashboard with buyer acquisition, observed successful jobs, repeat use, checkout outcomes and scoped revenue. Keep shipping counters as supporting evidence.

correction.title: The previous $38 MCP sales claim was incorrect
correction.text: The two referenced Stripe records are real paid $4.99 subscriptions on zovo.one, not $19 MCP purchases. Neither has an MCP price, product metadata or MCP line-item name. They do not validate MCP demand or MCP license fulfillment. The old note is retained with a prominent correction.

decision: Pause new server expansion as the default revenue strategy. Focus the next seven-day commercial test on the invoice-review workflow for bookkeepers/AP operators who already use a compatible assistant.

next_test.measure: Count an actual relevant operator with a supplied, permitted or redacted batch and an observed completed review. Exclude agents, crawlers, fixture data and directory accepts.
next_test.gate: 10 observed trials; diagnose installation and input friction for each failed attempt.

next_test.action: Test repeat use and the existing paid reason
next_test.measure: Ask why a user would return, whether more saved reports matters, and what prevents purchase. Record the answer; do not infer it from a click.
next_test.gate: 3 participants return with a second batch and at least 1 independent buyer pays the current offer. These are proposed decision thresholds, not forecasts.

next_test.measure: If 10 qualified users cannot be recruited, change the acquisition approach. If they try but do not return, change the workflow. If they return but do not pay, change the paid offer.
next_test.gate: No broad product expansion until buyer acquisition, repeat value and a paid outcome are observed. A week with too few trials is inconclusive, not product rejection.

limits: No Checkout, payment, email, account or production-code changes were made by this review.
All available completed Checkout history is not every payment channel or a lifetime net-profit audit. Telegram/other payment rails and total agent/hosting costs are unreconciled.
Google search analytics endsOctober 13; new October 16 products have not had a meaningful postlaunch observation period.
A tested payment-entry path does not prove live paid fulfillment or inbox delivery.
The broader release estate was 176 failed checks/28 gaps at its last October 16 checkpoint, including 54 version assertions; this review did not rerun it.

indexation.summary: Fresh Google inspection finds duplicate review and matcher discovered but not indexed; the new guide is still unknown. Homepage remains indexed. Discovery improved from unknown for two products, but neither has an indexed-page result.
